extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on calculation, extension, resetting, and restart of reply periods during patent prosecution, and rules/processes for express or formal abandonment (including petitions, fees, and timing constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) — maximum statutory limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) may be obtained to extend the period for reply; however, in no case can any extension carry the date for reply beyond the maximum period of SIX MONTHS set by statute (35 U.S.C. 133).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be accompanied by the appropriate fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(a). The date on which the reply, the petition, and the fee have been filed is the date of the reply and the date for determining the period of extension and the corresponding amount of the fee due. Although 37 CFR 1.136(a) provides for payment of up to five months of extension, applicant is advised that no extension can carry the date for reply beyond the six-month statutory maximum. Examiner Note: 37 CFR 1.136(a) does not apply to reexamination proceedings or to litigation-related reissue applications; do not use the form paragraph in those cases. Enclose a photocopy of current fee schedule with action so applicant can determine required fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period procedures for a final rejection (3-month shortened period)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a final rejection sets a 3-month shortened statutory period and applicant initially replies within 2 months, but the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the end of the 3-month period, the period for reply for purposes of determining the amount of any extension fee will be the date the Office mails the advisory action, but cannot extend beyond six months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must include the specified warning language in each final rejection indicating the 3-month shortened statutory period and that if a first reply is filed within two months and an advisory action is not mailed until after the end of three months, the shortened period will expire on the date the advisory action is mailed and any extension fee will be calculated from that mailing date. Examples given: if advisory mailed before end of 3 months, shortened period expires at 3 months; if mailed after, it expires on advisory mailing date. See MPEP § 710.01(a) and MPEP § 706.07(f). In no event will the statutory period for reply expire later than six months from the mailing date of the final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time to submit affidavits after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicants request extensions of time after final rejection to submit an affidavit, granting the extension is without prejudice to the examiner’s right to question why the affidavit is now necessary and was not earlier presented; if the showing is insufficient, the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit notwithstanding the grant of extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting the extension serves merely to keep the application from becoming abandoned while allowing the applicant an opportunity to present the affidavit or take other action. Prosecution to save the application from abandonment must include timely, complete and proper action as required by 37 CFR 1.113. Affidavits submitted after final rejection are subject to the same treatment as amendments after final rejection (see 37 CFR 1.116(c)). Admission or refusal to admit the affidavit, and related proceedings, shall not operate to save the application from abandonment unless proper procedures are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extensions after payment of the issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory (nonextendable) time period for payment of the issue fee is 3 months from the date of the Notice of Allowance (35 U.S.C. 151); extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) or (b) are NOT available to correct informalities once allowance issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If informalities such as drawing corrections are outstanding at allowance, applicants will be notified on PTOL-37 and must correct such informalities and pay the issue fee and publication fee within 3 months. If a Notice Requiring Inventor’s Oath or Declaration (PTOL-2306) is sent with the Notice of Allowability, required oath/declaration must be submitted no later than payment of the issue fee. See 35 U.S.C. 115(f). After payment of issue fee, only limited remedies (e.g., petitions under 37 CFR 1.313(c) or 1.183) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two different reply periods running — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When two different periods for reply are running against an application (the regular statutory period and a limited period set in a subsequent Office action), the running of the first period is not suspended nor affected by an ex parte limited time action or by an appeal therefrom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are exceptions (e.g., suggested claims — see MPEP Chapter 2300). The controlling period depends on the specific actions and dates in the file; examiners should follow applicable precedent and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copying patent claims — controlling date when claims copied from a patent are rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: Where in an application claims are copied from a patent and all of these claims are rejected, resulting in two different periods for reply, the date of the last unanswered Office action on the claims other than the copied patent claims is the controlling date of the statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Ex parte Milton, 63 USPQ 132 (P.O. Super Exam. 1938). See also MPEP Chapter 2300 for related practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period ending on Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: When the day or the last day for taking any action or paying any fee in the USPTO falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the action may be taken or fee paid on the next succeeding business day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday (35 U.S.C. 21; 37 CFR 1.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calendar days are intended when periods are specified. If a provisional 12‑month pendency date falls on a weekend/holiday, extend to next business day (37 CFR 1.7(b)). Lists federal holidays under 5 U.S.C. 6103(a) and explains when observance shifts (e.g., when holiday falls on Sunday or Saturday). Example provided showing extension to next business day when a 3‑month shortened statutory period expiry falls on Saturday and Monday is a federal holiday. When an amendment is filed one or two days late, ascertain whether the last day was weekend/holiday and whether filed on next business day; endorsements should indicate receipt date and that it was filed on the succeeding business day. See MPEP § 711.04(a) for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations when a reply period will be reset or restarted due to Office error
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an Office action contains an error that affects applicant’s ability to reply and this error is called to the Office’s attention within one month of the mail date, the Office will restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date the error is corrected (if applicant requests). If the error is called to attention within the reply period but more than one month after mailing, the Office will set a new period substantially equal to the time remaining in the reply period, but the new period must be at least one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of errors: invalid citations that are clearly erroneous (reference does not exist), illegible Office action or portion (garbled text), non-English Office action, or non-patent literature/foreign references not being provided (see MPEP § 707.05(a)). Where an action is remailed, applicant's period for reply restarts from the re-mailing date (MPEP § 707.13). A supplementary action explaining references more explicitly establishes a new date for the statutory period. If the error is called to attention after expiration of the reply period, the period will not be restarted and any appropriate extension fee is required. See MPEP §§ 505, 512, 513 for date stamping.

rubrics_metrics.name: e-Office Action program — email notification and resetting time periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If a customer registered in e-Office Action did not receive an email notification or received it late relative to the mailroom/notification date, the participant should contact the Patent Electronic Business Center (Patent EBC); the Office will send an email notification if one was not previously sent and restart any period for reply (except the 63‑day period under 37 CFR 90.3) when the Office sends the email notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office did send email notifications to each designated address, it will not send a new notification and any time period for reply will not be restarted. If an email notification is a few days later than the mailroom/notification date and the participant contacts Patent EBC within one month from the email date, the Office will reset the time period for reply (except for the 63‑day period under 37 CFR 90.3) to the original email date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to restart period for reply due to late receipt of Office action — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the previously set period for reply to run from the date of receipt at the correspondence address when the following are met: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of date of receipt at correspondence address; (B) a substantial portion of the set reply period had elapsed on the date of receipt (e.g., at least 1 month of a 2‑ or 3‑month reply period); and (C) petition includes evidence showing date of receipt at the correspondence address and a statement explaining how evidence establishes that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible evidence examples: copy of Office action stamped with date of receipt at correspondence address, copy of envelope showing date of receipt, etc. There is no statutory requirement to reset a shortened statutory period longer than 30 days, but the above procedures are available when substantial portion elapsed. If an action was received with less than two months remaining in a 3‑month shortened period, the period may be restarted; if between two and three months remaining, reset only in extraordinary situations (e.g., complex action suggesting comparative data). Authority to decide such petitions has been delegated to Technology Center Directors when the Office action was mailed by a TC. See Notice “Petition to reset a period for response due to late receipt of a PTO action,” 1160 OG 14 (March 1, 1994).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to restart period for reply due to postmark date later than mail date printed on Office action — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will grant a petition to restart the previously set period for reply to run from the postmark date shown on the Office mailing envelope when: (A) petition filed within 2 weeks of date of receipt at correspondence address; (B) the reply period was for payment of the issue fee, or the reply period set was 1 month or 30 days; and (C) petition includes (1) evidence showing date of receipt at correspondence address, (2) copy of the envelope showing the postmark date, and (3) a statement setting forth the date of receipt and stating the Office action was received in the postmarked envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.8 and 1.10 apply regarding filing within 2 weeks. The showings may not be sufficient if circumstances point to delay after receipt rather than delay in the mail or Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.135 abandonment for failure to reply and required content of prosecution to save application
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time period provided under §§ 1.134 and 1.136, the application will become abandoned (37 CFR 1.135). Prosecution to save an application from abandonment must include such complete and proper reply as the condition of the application may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission of, or refusal to admit, any amendment after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action, or any related proceedings, will not operate to save the application from abandonment. When reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application and some matter or compliance was inadvertently omitted, applicant may be given a new time period under § 1.134 to supply the omission (37 CFR 1.135(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment formal requirements and effects (37 CFR 1.138)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be expressly abandoned by filing a written declaration of abandonment identifying the application, signed by a party authorized under § 1.33(b)(1) or (b)(3). Express abandonment may not be recognized by the Office before the date of issue or publication unless actually received by appropriate officials in time to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing methods: electronically using USPTO patent electronic filing system or mailed to Mail Stop Express Abandonment. If petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) is used to avoid publication, submit electronically if projected publication is less than 3 months away to increase chance of timely recognition. Office will acknowledge proper express abandonment by using Notice of Abandonment form PTO-1432 and checking appropriate boxes; if letter does not comply, send fully explanatory letter. A letter of express abandonment not timely filed (because not filed within period for reply) is not acceptable to expressly abandon the application and should be placed in the file but not formally entered. An amendment canceling all claims is not express abandonment; such amendment is regarded nonresponsive and not bona fide attempt (see Exxon v. Phillips). An attorney/agent not of record may file withdrawal of appeal except where withdrawal results in abandonment; then withdrawal is express abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment after payment of issue fee — additional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a letter of express abandonment is submitted in an allowed application after payment of the issue fee, the express abandonment must be accompanied by a petition to withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c) and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h); the petition and abandonment must be received and the petition granted before the date of issue to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address petition to Office of Petitions. Filing options: mail to Mail Stop Petition, fax, hand-carry, or submit electronically via USPTO filing system. Applicants are strongly encouraged to e‑file, fax, or hand‑carry to allow sufficient processing time. If 37 CFR 1.313 precludes giving effect to an express abandonment, remedy is petition under 37 CFR 1.183 showing extraordinary situation where justice requires suspension of 37 CFR 1.313. If petition and letter received in time and petition granted, acknowledgement will be by Office of Data Management after petition is granted. See MPEP §§ 711.05 and 1308.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition timing to avoid publication of application
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) will not stop publication unless recognized and acted on by the Pre‑Grant Publication Division in sufficient time to avoid publication; generally, declaration of express abandonment and petition must be received by appropriate officials more than four weeks prior to projected publication date to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition filed within four weeks of projected publication date is unlikely to avoid publication. Withdrawal from issue after payment of issue fee may not prevent publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b). Technical preparations for publication usually begin four months prior to the projected publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of search fee and excess claims fee via express abandonment (37 CFR 1.138(d)) — timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a refund of the search fee and excess claims fee paid in an application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and § 1.53(b) on or after December 8, 2004, an applicant must submit a declaration of express abandonment by way of a petition under 37 CFR 1.138(d) before an examination has been made of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on any certificate of mailing or transmission under § 1.8 is not taken into account in determining whether petition was filed before an examination. If the request for refund is not filed with the declaration or within two months from the date the declaration was filed, the Office may retain the entire search fee and excess claims fee; the two‑month period is not extendable. A petition under 1.138(d) will be granted only if filed before an examination has been made; an examination is counted when an action is shown in the One Patent Data Portal (PDP) as having been counted (status higher than 031). If PDP status is higher than 031 before or on the day the petition was filed, the petition will be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'examination has been made' for purposes of 37 CFR 1.138(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'examination has been made of the application' is shown by an action (e.g., restriction/election requirement, requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, first Office action on the merits, notice of allowability/allowance, or action under Ex parte Quayle) being shown in the One Patent Data Portal as having been counted; PDP shows status higher than 031 once an action has been counted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an action is counted on the same day a petition under 1.138(d) is filed, the petition is not considered filed before an examination. The date on any certificate of mailing or transmission under § 1.8 is not taken into account for this determination. Technical preparations for publication begin about four months before projected publication; petitions may not be effective to stop publication unless processed before that stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended forms and filing methods for express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms PTO/AIA/24 (or PTO/SB/24 for pre‑Sept 16, 2012) may be used for filing a letter of express abandonment or a letter in favor of a continuing application; PTO/AIA/24B (or PTO/SB/24B) and PTO/AIA/24A (or PTO/SB/24A) are referenced for related filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office recommends use of the USPTO patent electronic filing system; when publication is imminent, electronic submission increases chance of timely processing. See MPEP § 711.01 subsection V for form reproduction and guidance.
